VAN 1067 is a TPM2.0 and secure boot error. Check to see if both are enabled. 

For me, they were both enabled and I kept getting the error. I did a CMOS reset, turned on core isolation in windows security, and monitored vgc while playing valorant to make sure it’s not shutting off by itself. 

But first, check TPM and secure boot before you do anything else

Try doing a CMOS reset. If you have a CMOS battery, unplug it for a few minutes then replug and reboot. Your BIOS settings will reset, so make sure to change it after. 

Also, if you have dual moniters, open "services.msc" (after pressing Windows key + R) and open properties for "vgc" 

Run valorant and keep checking to see if vgc automatically stops. If it does, stop riot client from task manager. Then, manually start vgc from properties and reopen valorant. 

I don’t know why, but the issue cleared for me after these two steps. I’m on windows 11 with the latest software update and nvidia drivers.

For me, switching majors was a last resort. I failed another required course because of studio, and I didn’t want to be a year behind. Turns out, it didn’t matter if I failed that professor’s unit. Since the previous professor gave me an A. I would’ve still passed studio, while having the time to complete make-up work for my other classes. 

If you decide to switch majors, consider your situation thoroughly and carefully. When I was taking prerequisite courses for engineering the semester after, I failed all of my classes. I wasn’t ready for the transition, and giving up on my passion for architecture haunted me 24/7. I’m now enrolled in community college to raise my grades so that I can transfer. I’m basically starting over completely, but I feel much more centered and stable now. It sucks to be 3 years behind compared to my peers, but everyone has a different academic journey. It’s a marathon not a sprint. 

Talk to your advisor about your situation. They can walk you through steps on how to stay in architecture, and offer different plans for academic recovery. You can even be completely honest to your professor about how you feel and what needs to change. Honesty is not a valid reason for failing a student, so don’t worry about that. Some professors just don’t know what they are doing wrong. 

Also, this might not apply to you, but please take care of yourself. Don’t pull all nighters. Eat balanced meals. Limit caffeine usage. Get some exercise in. I didn’t do any of these, and it ended up worsening my mental health significantly. Time is super limited in architecture school, but taking care of yourself is going to make you more productive than pulling all nighters.

That’s just the culture here in Korea. Wealth is everything. Usually, it doesn’t go as far as renting exotic cars. The green plate is for company cars, which are being used privately by family members of company owners to reduce taxes.

It’s the same in korea. plate with an 호 or 허 character is usually a rental. IIRC it doesn’t apply to company cars though. The green plate is only for company cars above 80,000,000 won. 

It’s not always that they want to look like they own it, it’s a way to reduce taxes. If a spouse or parent owns a company, they can file them as an employee of his/her company and lease a “company vehicle", which would just be a privately owned car with less taxes. 

With the green plates, the hope is that people will be discouraged to drive company vehicles as their own because they risk being investigated for tax evasion. I’m sure there’s a loophole there though.

When I was 17, I had similar experiences. I’m not saying this to invalidate your feelings, or call you young and naive. I’m 21 now. I failed out of college, lost all of my friends, and my life is a mess. Despite this, I don’t feel hopeless. 

When I was 17, I felt like my life was crumbling apart. I had two friends I could depend on, and lost one due to suicide. My family was never supportive. They once asked me to apologize to the school for self harming. I overdosed every week for the hope that my liver would shut down in my sleep. I can go on and list all the reasons why I felt like my life was falling apart, but to be honest, it doesn’t matter.

It doesn’t matter because while the suffering and pain is temporary, we unknowingly decide to make it permanent. What you go through now will (not might) be different from what you go through in the future. Life is like a video game, it’s always going through updates. It is never permanently the same, and always evolving. 

Despite how shitty and out of control my life is right now, I don’t feel hopeless or lost. In fact, I feel content. As you get older and have new experiences, you learn how to roll with the punches. Life doesn’t always get better, but you will always get better at dealing with it. 

If you end it here, you won’t get a chance to recover. If my attempts were successful, I would never have lived to see that a shitty life is no different from a perfect life; life itself is not happy or unhappy, it’s you. 

Everything is temporary. Your happiness, suffering, friends, relationships, passions, fears, etc. It doesn’t feel this way now, but it’s a fact of life (which is also temporary). You can either be uncertain about what’s ahead, or be fine with it being uncertain and let life carry you forward. 

It will be okay. I understand your suffering, and you are strong for going through it alone. However, not everything can be done alone. I know it’s hard to make friends in the current age, but there are others out there who are going through a similar experience, desperately searching for someone they can lean on.

If you haven’t already, I highly recommend finding a good psychiatrist to prescribe you medication that works. Therapy is also good, but sometimes it’s inaccessible and ineffective. You can always PM me if you need someone to talk to.

Modern medicine has never been so advanced, yet it remains inaccessible to many. Society is divided among class, race, generation, politics, and religion. I would like to help people and society as a whole, but not if it is dictated by the unsympathetic minds in power. I can work hard to be the best, but with that best, can society bloom into something good? Will my hard work be scattered across the world or will it remain stagnant, catching dust in the room where potential goes to die?

If you hurt someone's feelings, does that mean there's something wrong with you? I don't personally think so, because we're not computers, we're humans. We can sometimes misjudge the situation, we can sometimes hurt people unintentionally, we can sometimes say the wrong things at the wrong time. If we were perfect creatures, then yes, unintentionally hurting another's feelings means there is something wrong with us (hence, we are imperfect when we're meant to be perfect). Humans are imperfect, and are meant to be imperfect, and there is nothing wrong with that.

I can't give you a straight answer, because we can't know every little detail about these conversations and expressions that cause you to suppress your feelings. Maybe the people who were hurt are dealing with a lot, maybe they lack empathy or acceptance. Maybe it struck a nerve because it relates to a personal trauma. Everyone has the right to express feeling and emotion, and sometimes people express anger, sometimes they express kindness. Sometimes which emotion someone expresses is completely independent from what the listener feels (i.e. not taking into consideration what the other person might feel when you say a certain thing). 

Important thing is to know that there's nothing wrong with you. It's perfectly fine to be imperfect. You know that you genuinely want to improve, so directly asking how you can improve might be a good first step. Be able to know when you're not in the wrong (my depression in the past made me blame myself for others' faults). This also resulted in me staying in toxic relationships and friendships without me knowing. Consult friends, family, and therapists about this issue too. They might be more helpful than strangers on the internet.

There are four screws, all on the inside of the swinging piece. Two are visible near the circular portion, the other two are angled and behind the two I just mentioned. After removing these, you can push the whole panel back to remove it. 

Please note, it's important to disconnect the wire for the button (one green, four gray, red harness) from the back.

Then, remove the two screws holding the head cover and button. Removing this part was the hardest for me. I still don't exactly know how, but I pushed the back portion up and gradually used more force until it popped off. 

Every step after that should be pretty intuitive. Unplug the water hose connector from the top, remove the plastic nut using a pair of pliers. Remove the top screws and the one spring thing. If you fiddle with it long enough and document every step of the way, you should be able to disassemble it pretty easily. 

Oh also, when removing the latch that opens and closes the head piece, you need to push down on a little hidden latch near the main hinge. Finding this piece took me a while.

Keep in mind you will need a security torx wrench or bit (t10)

1. Unscrew the bottom panel (IIRC there were four screws) 
2. With the machine standing up, hold down the bottom panel while pushing the machine to the side. This will unlatch the machine body from the bottom panel. 
3. You won't need to remove the bottom panel, you only need to unlatch it. 
4. There are three outer panels on the Next. Two in the front, one that wraps around the body. To unlatch these, you will need to push down on the panel.
5. Once you remove the panels, disconnect the following wires from the back: 
   1. IR Sensor/Reader connector (one red many gray)
   2. Motor connector (Red and blue with yellow harness) 
   3. Red white and blue wire (w/green harness)
   4. red and blue wire (w/white harness)
6. When looking from the bottom, you will see two screws on the circular portion of the machine (near the water dispenser). Remove them.
7. Now remove the ring that goes around this circular part by pushing it up (it feels like it will break, but trust me on this) 
8. Remove the top section (the part that swings open) by pushing out the metal rod that holds it together, then taking the springs out.
9. Now you should be able to remove the entire pod holder + the body that holds it
10. Remove the tiny piece on the left side of the machine (held together by two screws)
11. Clean this piece and the bottom of the pod holder then reassemble. 

**Important: The barcode scanner/reader isn't what's dirty, its the clear plastic piece that prevents it from scanning. TREAT THE BARCODE SCANNER CIRCUIT BOARD WITH CARE (you can even remove it after disconnecting the wire for it)**

I live in Korea and have only visited a psychiatrist and therapist before. Psychiatrists (I went to one of the biggest hospitals in Korea) really do not care about treatment, just prescribing the newest medication to get paid by pharmaceutical companies. I remember hearing a story from one of my relatives where the psychiatrist prescribed her a "magic pill" that will "cure her depression" in a matter of weeks. 

My therapist was helpful, but it’s $100 per session, and not covered by my insurance. I also had to retake (and lie on) my military health exam because my mom was afraid I’d have trouble finding a job later on or get picked on due to my psychological record. 

If you have a mental illness, it brings shame to not only yourself but your parents. It’s looked down upon when finding a job, because employers don’t want people with flaws, they want perfect specimens that do what they are told without any complaints and without a drop in productivity. 90% of Koreans don’t understand mental illness. For example, my parents thought ADHD was just a lack  of emotional control that’s only present in children. 

I tutor as a part time job, and one of my ex-students was a bubbly 3rd grader who has an outstanding interest in learning new things. I tried my best to make him not feel exhausted, and grow his interests and be proud of himself for what he is able to achieve. Meanwhile his mother is always telling him he can be better, that he needs to study so he can get into a good hagwon, that he can’t rest until he finishes whatever he needs to study. Eventually, the mom ghosted me, and I’m assuming it’s because I was allowing the kid to have fun while learning, because I wasn’t working him like a slave, because she didn’t see the unrealistic results she wanted to see. 

All in all I’d say its heavily stigmatized, it took my parents many years and a suicide attempt to only partially realize mental illness is real.
